deep.reconstruction:
This is a page of raw geomagnetic observing data and arithmetic from the Göttingen Magnetic Observatory. The previous page carries the date Oct. 25 [1835]. There is no mathematical derivation, only data reduction.

(A) Left block (ink). The first column is a list of clock times in minutes and seconds: 32'49.2", 33'32.7", 34'15.8", ..., 44'20.7". The same list appears in the margin of the previous page.
- The successive differences are about 43.0–43.6 s, mostly 43.0–43.1 s. Examples: 34'15.8" → 34'58.9" = 43.1 s; 39'18.7" → 40'1.7" = 43.0 s.
- The gap marked with dashes, 37'8.0" → 38'35.6" = 87.6 s, is two such intervals. So one epoch is deliberately skipped there.
- These look like epochs of equally spaced readings timed to the needle's oscillation. That fits Gauss's procedure of reading the magnetometer at fixed multiples of its period.
- Against each epoch are two scale readings (e.g. 22.1 / 26.0, 20.9 / 25.0, ...). The hundreds, and probably the tens, of the scale divisions are suppressed.
- A third column with three decimals follows (10.217, 10.600, 10.800, 10.287, 9.937, ...). The decimals suggest means over a varying number of readings. Examples: 9.937 ≈ 9.9375 = n/16; 10.458 ≈ n/24; 10.767 ≈ n/3; 9.972 ≈ n/36. This column could be either such means or the readings of a second instrument (e.g. the bifilar intensity variometer). The page does not let me fix the rule, and I do not assert one.
- The extra rows at top and bottom are probably additional readings outside the timed list: 10.9; 27.6/27.0/10.217; 23.6/28.8/10.600; and at the end 25.3/9.972 and 26.0.

(B) Right block (pencil). This is the standard reduction of a deflection or reversal experiment, the same scheme as on the next page (pairs summed, then differences of sums).
- Group I: 1242.4 + 1248.8 = 2491.2 and 769.7 + 776.6 = 1546.3.
- Group II: 1238.3 + 1251.0, entered as 2489.4 (the true sum is 2489.3). Also 766.8 + 775.5 = 1542.3.
- Alternating (interleaved) differences of the sums:
  - 2491.2 − 1546.3 = 944.9
  - 2489.4 − 1546.3 = 943.1
  - 2489.4 − 1542.3 = 947.1
- Mean (my reading of the entry '945 0333'): (944.9 + 943.1 + 947.1)/3 = 945.0333.
- Half: 945.0333/2 = 472.517, written in parentheses.
- The difference of the two-reading sums is twice the difference between the two bar positions. So 472.517 is the full swing in scale divisions between the two positions, and half of that again is the single deflection.
- Interleaving the differences A1−B1, A2−B1, A2−B2 cancels the linear drift of the declination during the experiment. This is Gauss's usual practice.
- '8,3' (twice, once with 'Th') is a thermometer reading, 8.3°, presumably Réaumur.
- 2018.5, 2016.9, 2017.8 are further readings (mean 2017.73, not written).
- The bottom pencil notes (8480, 4600, 1700, with words resembling 'afstand?'/'been') are unclear and may be in another hand.
errors: 1238.3 + 1251.0 = 2489.3, but 2489.4 is written. Either the first reading is really 1238.4 (misread or ambiguous digit), or Gauss slipped by 0.1. The later differences 943.1 and 947.1 consistently use 2489.4.

The left-hand time list is regular, but one interval (41'27.4" − 40'44.7" = 42.7 s) is slightly short. Since the '40.44.7' entry is overwritten, this is a reading or observing irregularity, not a computational error.
